title.narrative: Percentage of key community CSOs rated high on good management & governance systems in an external project evaluation

description.narrative: Good management and governance indices 1. Rule of lawenforceale constitution 2. Transparencymeetings & feedback mechanisms 3. Accountaabilityregular meetings, financial reports, clear responsibilities of roles of leaders 4. Participationmembers in decison making 5. Equity & inclusivenessgender considerations 6. Efficiency & effectivenessplans and budgets 7. Conflict resoultion 8. Legal regal registrations

comment.narrative: Percentange calculated as total number of community CSOs rated high on good management governance systems over 27 targeted community CSOs multipled by 100

Based on the Good Governance Index which assesses the following elements effectiveness conflict management accountability participation and equity 51 of the CSOs have been rated high on good management governance systems. These include River Ranch LDC Malala DRRC River Ranch IMC Shashe IST Jalukange ICS Dendele LDC Masera LDC Ward 4 DRRC Ward 4 LDC Ndambe 1 ICS Ndambe 2 ICS District Agriculture Union Ward 10 DRR and Kwalu ICS. This was attributed to the regular meetings with members engagement and participation of CSO members defined governance structures and improve financial management systems.

title.narrative: 2.Improved performance of IMCs, DCAs, DRR Committees and DTCs in the development of resilient AVCs

description.narrative: 2.Improved performance of IMCs, DCAs, DRR Committees and DTCs in the development of resilient AVCs

title.narrative: Percentage of farmers served by key community CSOs confirming that they have access to and are benefitting from resilient agricultural value chains

description.narrative: Resilient value chains are agricultural value chains with the capacity to continue and develop in the face of disturbances Beneffiting referes to livelihoods income,employment

comment.narrative: Total number of farmers indicating access to resilient agricultural value chains and are expressing satisfaction of the services provided divided by total interviewd farmers 100

75 113 of the 150 members served by CSOs as per survey results confirmed that they were benefitting from resilient agriculture value chains. This is mostly attributed to plot holders in irrigation schemes benefitting from the sugar bean contract with SeedCo and PPCP with BBJ on oranges horticulture farmers interfacing with restaurants and fruit and vegetable retailers as well as livestock producers benefitting from access to input suppliers through linkages such as dipping chemicals from Coopers acaricides from Agroshape as well as organised Diptank sales and linkages with offtakers Matebeleland beef company Bulawayo Abbatoirs and MC Meats.

title.narrative: 3.Enhanced capacity of IMCs, DCAs, DRR Committees and LDCs to influence key policies related to agriculture and resilience

description.narrative: 3.Enhanced capacity of IMCs, DCAs, DRR Committees and LDCs to influence key policies related to agriculture and resilience

title.narrative: Percentage of leaders in key community CSOs confirming that they are involved in processes to influence key policies related to agriculture and resilience

description.narrative: CSO leaders referes to committee members for each of the targeted CSOs (IMCs,DCAs,LDCs & DRR committees) Process to influence policies include:1. Participation in policy audits & review of existing policies 2. Participation at multistakeholder roundtables 3. Involvement in online platforms created to discuss policies related to agriculture 4. Participation in the development of policy briefs

comment.narrative: Percentage calculated as total number of leaders in key community CSOs declaringperceiving they are invoved in processes to influence key policies related agriculture resilience divided by total number of leaders in targeted key community CSOs100

127 of the 228 CSO leaders 55 confirmed that they were involved in processes related to influencing key policies related to agriculture. During the preliminary discussion in preparation to the endline evaluation and monitoring visits CSO leaders highlighted that were capacitated to undertake conducting a policy audit for policies affecting smallholder agriculture and participated on multistakeholder roundtable. These also participated in the development of a policy brief to be presented to local authorities. Moreover CSO leaders from the different CSO categories participated at budget consultation fora spearheaded by local authorities at ward level and constantly engage in dialogue on the established online platform.

title.narrative: Percentage of CSO members confirming that the capacity of their organisations has improved

description.narrative: The indicator tracks capacity and ability of CSOs members to provide services to clients such as trainings, skills, resources by analyzing the satisfaction of CSO members as client

comment.narrative: Number of respondents CSOs members expressing satisfaction for positive consideration of their CSO capacity total n. of respondent100

The third indicator measuring the achievement of this result was fulfilled as 75 113 of the 150 beneficiaries interviewed during the final evaluation and periodic project monitoring surveys confirmed that the capacity of their organisation has improved. On assessing organisational capacity the following parameters of CSO capacity were considered as measured by organisational resources assets materials organisational structure protocols and processes organisational knowledge skills and competencies and partnerships relationships and connections. Beneficiaries alluded to the formalisation of their CSOs which gave them the capacity to enter in to agreements and allow them to engage in resource mobilisation activities. Beneficiaries in CSOs that were awarded with third party grants referred to the functional pieces of productive infrastructure for resilience that were established. Skills and knowledge attained in the trainings and exchange visits were also mentioned during interviews to have improved CSO organisational capacity.

title.narrative: Percentage or number of key community CSOs demonstrating institutional and economic sustainability

description.narrative: 1. Economic and Institutional sustainability Key community CSOs are vibrant effective and legally binding and can interface with formal sector and other stakeholders.They have a clear vision and well articulated business plans for their organisations.They have regular ,meetings with members and have updated financial records.Have members that are motivated to participate in the affairs of the CSOs and have positive appreciation of the quality of services offered by CSOs

comment.narrative: Total number of key community CSOs demonstrating institutional and economic sustainability divided number of targeted key community CSOs multiplied by 100

The first indicator measuring the achievement of the project specific objective was partially fulfilled. Based on the adapted version of the institutional sustainability index which measures the following dimensions legal organisational capacity financial viability the CSOs ability to influence public opinion and public policy the CSOs ability to provide goods and services support services available to the CSO and societys perception on the CSO 8 of the 27 CSOs namely ward 6 DRRC River Ranch LDC River Ranch ICS Jalukange ICS Ward 4 DRRC Masera LDC Dendele LDC and Shashe Trust have achieved institutional and economic sustainability. This is attributed to among other factors the blended suite of capacity development activities inclusive of management and governance trainings provision of tools of work evidencebased policy advocacy training and economic strengthening activities supported through the provision of thirdparty grants. Evidence from MEAL reports confirm that the mentioned CSOs have aquired new skills demonstrated attitude change and operationalised the aquired skills. The 8 CSOs successfully improved their financial collection strategic income generative activities to improve revenue generation to meet CSO needs and feedback practices hence deepened participation trust and voice from membership. The formal registration of these CSOs compelled compliance to organizational statutes including their constitution thus driving commitment cooperation and equity on resource sharing and utilization by all CSO members. The CSOs now have binding statutes and bylaws spelling out roles responsibilities authority and membership. However maintenance of irrigation infrastructure and electricity power access for irrigation remains the major challenge that may jeopardize the project gains on building CSO economic sustainability.
Please note that Current Value is not the one formally submitted with the Year 2 Narrative Interim Report. Current Value is updated to the last internal Indicator Tracking Table

title.narrative: Percentage or number of key community CSOs demonstrating institutional and economic sustainability

description.narrative: 1. Economic and Institutional sustainability Key community CSOs are vibrant effective and legally binding and can interface with formal sector and other stakeholders.They have a clear vision and well articulated business plans for their organisations.They have regular ,meetings with members and have updated financial records.Have members that are motivated to participate in the affairs of the CSOs and have positive appreciation of the quality of services offered by CSOs

comment.narrative: Total number of key community CSOs demonstrating institutional and economic sustainability divided number of targeted key community CSOs multiplied by 100

The first indicator measuring the achievement of the project specific objective was partially fulfilled. Based on the adapted version of the institutional sustainability index which measures the following dimensions legal organisational capacity financial viability the CSOs ability to influence public opinion and public policy the CSOs ability to provide goods and services support services available to the CSO and societys perception on the CSO 8 of the 27 CSOs namely ward 6 DRRC River Ranch LDC River Ranch ICS Jalukange ICS Ward 4 DRRC Masera LDC Dendele LDC and Shashe Trust have achieved institutional and economic sustainability. This is attributed to among other factors the blended suite of capacity development activities inclusive of management and governance trainings provision of tools of work evidencebased policy advocacy training and economic strengthening activities supported through the provision of thirdparty grants. Evidence from MEAL reports confirm that the mentioned CSOs have aquired new skills demonstrated attitude change and operationalised the aquired skills. The 8 CSOs successfully improved their financial collection strategic income generative activities to improve revenue generation to meet CSO needs and feedback practices hence deepened participation trust and voice from membership. The formal registration of these CSOs compelled compliance to organizational statutes including their constitution thus driving commitment cooperation and equity on resource sharing and utilization by all CSO members. The CSOs now have binding statutes and bylaws spelling out roles responsibilities authority and membership. However maintenance of irrigation infrastructure and electricity power access for irrigation remains the major challenge that may jeopardize the project gains on building CSO economic sustainability.
Please note that Current Value is not the one formally submitted with the Year 2 Narrative Interim Report. Current Value is updated to the last internal Indicator Tracking Table

title.narrative: Number of local authorities & community CSOs reporting increased interinstitutional cooperation and effectiveness in promoting community development

description.narrative: Interinstitutional cooperationCSOs ability to cooperate and coordinate with local authorities and other palyers in planning & conducting review meetings, multistakeholder policy dialogues as well as any other community development initiatives

comment.narrative: sum of LA representatives CSO members reporting increased Interinstitutional cooperation and effectiveness total number of respondent100

The fourth indicator measuring the achievement of this result as cooperation among CSOs and authorities improved during the project life span. 7 DRR committees have been effectively coordinating with local authorities COVID19 response and flood preparedness particularly the RDC and the DDCs office. It is envisaged that through capacity building in evidencebased policy advocacy and provision of space for policy dialogue interinstitutional cooperation is set to increase among CSOs and with the local authorities. CSO members confirmed that they can freely walk in and discuss pertinent issues with policy makers. Particularly the 7 LDCs confirmed to be cooperating with BBRDC on livestock markets and marketing issues
